text: Company uses local suppliers and sub-contractors and employs locally as much as possible.
Localising the supply chain reduces shipping/storage, emissions and energy usage and supply chain costs.
The company has successfully completed over 200 projects (apartment blocks, housing schemes, nursing homes, schools, office blocks, large industrial and warehousing).

text: Managing Director has over 30 years' experience in the construction industry and previously worked for two of Ireland's largest construction companies.
The Managing Director oversees every aspect of projects including procurement, hiring/managing project team and ensuring compliance with building and safety regulations.
Commercial Director has over 30 years' experience as a Quantity Surveyor and joined Ormonde in 2015.
The Commercial Director manages the Estimating Department in delivery of tender submissions and has negotiated several significant residential, commercial and primary care centre buildings.
Contracts Director has over 20 years' experience, is degree qualified in Civil and Transportation Engineering, joined in 2005 and was appointed Contracts Director in 2017.
Contracts Director is responsible for all site management teams and project delivery compliant with Building and HSEQ requirements.
The team page lists a Managing Director, Contracts Director, Commercial Director and Commercial Manager.
A quantity surveyor's duties include ensuring compliance with the Building Control Amendment Regulations (BCAR).
Ormonde manages every aspect of commercial projects from pre-construction through to completion.
Ormonde delivers fitout projects and operates 'at scale'.
Design-build delivery: the company finds it often translates to shorter schedules and lower project costs.
Ormonde provides design and build services.
Ormonde provides healthcare/primary care facilities with 'highly qualified teams'; healthcare is a key market.
Ormonde provides education facilities, including work in live school environments.
Ormonde provides industrial project services including programme management and cost analysis.
Ormonde provides residential services: project managing large social housing programmes, scheme design and placemaking; development team initiating new schemes.
Residential clients can be assured the finished result is delivered on time and budget and to the highest quality (reliable accommodation models).
Health and safety: tool box talks, safety inductions, training and daily whiteboard meetings are used on projects.
All sites are regularly inspected by the company's H&S team for compliance with company procedures and legislative requirements.
Health & safety is at the heart of everything the company does; safety standards are constantly evaluated.
Committed to providing the necessary resources to eliminate injury and incidents on all projects.
Core objective: every individual working on Ormonde sites returns home safely and leaves with a sense of wellbeing.
Quality objectives and control processes are defined and implemented; each project has a risk management plan (identify, prioritise, contingency, revisit and revise).
The company uses the latest software to track changes in a live environment so all parties work on the same consolidated information; CAD is used in design.

Sustainability statement commitments: comply fully with legal requirements, assess environmental impacts and seek to reduce pollution, promote environmental and energy awareness through employee training, work with customers on sensitive choices, monitor progress, communicate policy to stakeholders.
Crokers Hill project used eco-friendly materials (recycled or locally sourced), recycling/reuse of construction debris, and regular inspections and training on health and safety.
Crokers Hill: over 88 housing units.
A residential project is described as 'over 70 housing units' (listing on residential page; project not named in extracted text).
College Park, Callan Road, Kilkenny City: 59 residential units (timber frame, 3 and 4-bed semi-detached and terraced, duplexes, apartments).
Castle Oaks: phased development of 77 mixed-tenure residential homes; Breagagh River site constraints; ESB overhead wires rerouted underground.
Castle Oaks next phase launching (upcoming).
Droughill Housing: 26 new residences (18 two-storey terraced and 8 single-storey semi-detached), 90 to 100 square metres each.
Market Square (Vignoles Gardens): Design and Build contract for 20 elderly houses and apartments incl. renovation of a derelict Protected Structure.
Walkin Street, Kilkenny City: 27 apartments, community centre, offices, underground car park, 3800m2 floor area, 4-storey over basement.
Walkin Street development is 'award winning' (award not named).
Kilkenny Primary Care: three-storey Primary Health Care centre, 5867m2 floor area, NZEB compliant, turnkey with furniture and fittings.
Thomastown Primary Care Centre: commissioned by the HSE, 3500 square metres, two-storey, Ladys Well St., Thomastown.
Callan Primary Care: Primary Care Centre and Neighbour Centre in Westcourt, Callan, with 3,000 sq ft GP surgery, fit-out to HSE standards.

Thomastown social and affordable housing: 42 units on a 1.24 hectare site at Abbeyhill, Ladywell Street, for Kilkenny County Council under Housing for All; Ormonde appointed contractor; expected completion early 2026.

refs.ref: sources/new-social-and-affordable-housing-scheme-in-kilkenny.html#L1031 (quoted statement attributed to the council's chief executive naming Ormonde)

text: Planning permission granted by Kilkenny County Council for a new primary care centre on Hebron Road, Kilkenny (89 parking spaces); Hebron Road Primary Care Centre and Housing is listed as upcoming.
Upcoming projects: Fethard Primary Care Centre, Thurles Housing, Williamstown Housing, Tullamore Warehouse 12, Thomastown Housing, Hebron Road Primary Care Centre and Housing.
Adamstown community centre: SDZ project, 15 months from planning submission to handover; built in a seven-month programme within budget; Ormonde managed precast works on a design and build basis.
Aras Brugha Hostel, Dungarvan: refurbishment, three-storey extension, M&E works; completed March 2019.
Bergins: 50,000 ft2 warehouse for Bergin Haulage at Purcellsinch Business Park, Kilkenny; 11m clear height; 8m high retaining walls.
Meubles: 100,000 sq ft retail showroom over two floors at Smithland's Retail Park, Kilkenny, built while the park stayed operational.
PRL Logistics Solutions: 30,000 sq ft high-bay warehouse built within a live bonded site.
Nowlan Park (UPMC Nowlan Park, Kilkenny GAA): new 4,000 all-seated covered stand, roof for Ardan Breathneach, County Board offices refurbishment; stadium fully operational during works.
Gowran Park racecourse (15 minutes from Kilkenny city): demolition of jockeys' weights room and new two-storey weight room building; limestone cladding; handover reported 8 October 2024.
Taxback: renovation of a three-storey 20,000 sq ft office block, delivered with a five-month completion deadline.
Powerscourt Distillery and Visitors Centre, Enniskerry, Co. Wicklow: Ormonde was Main Contractor; new 15m distillery building; restoration of 1730 mill house (protected structure).
Church of Oak Distillery (Ballykelly Distillery) near Monasterevin, Co. Kildare: demolition, asbestos removal, site works.
St. Gerard's Private School, Bray, Co. Wicklow: extension to Junior and Senior schools, fire remediation, all work in a live school with phased handover.
St. Teresian's School, Dublin 4: two-storey build, sports hall, brownfield site in a live school with phased handover.
Ormonde Construction took part in the Construction Industry Federation's International Women's Day event (7 March 2024) via a staff panel member.
A staff quantity surveyor works at Ormonde, joined after working at a local Kilkenny firm, England and Dublin (podcast feature, July 2024).
